OPENING

A tool cabinet that costs a few lakhs, against one that costs twenty.

ZOLLER's »toolOrganizer« sells into Indian machine shops at roughly ₹20 lakh a cabinet.c This is a working demonstrator of the same idea, built from 145.3 g of PLA, two hobby servos and a ₹600 microcontroller.

Every number on this page was printed by a script in the repository it links to. Where a figure came from a datasheet rather than a measurement, it is marked. Where the design failed an audit, the failure is on the page.

d datasheet · c claim · e estimate · unmarked = printed by a script here
Entry01/ 10
THE OBJECT

This is the machine, not a render.

Assembled from the same STLs that go to the printer. The drawer stroke is the mechanism's own: one half turn of the m1.25 × 16 pinion is π × 10.0 = 31.42 mm.

If both servos die, the drawers pull out by hand. There is no solenoid holding them shut.

Entry02/ 10
THE CLAIM

The expensive cabinet does not sense anything either.

No load cells. No cameras. No RFID. Inventory in a »toolOrganizer« is trust-basedc — the cabinet records that a drawer opened, not what left it.

What a shop is buying is controlled access and a record of who opened what. That is a lock, a database and a screen. It is not twenty lakhs of sensing, because there is no sensing.

This page will not claim the demonstrator senses anything either. It does not.

the argument the whole product rests on
Entry03/ 10
MECHANISM

Rack and pinion, straight off a servo horn.

Each drawer carries a toothed blade through a slot in the deck. A 16-tooth involute pinion on the servo horn drives it. No leadscrew, no belt, no bearings — two moving parts per drawer.

THE FINDING

An independent audit returned NO-GO.

The first mechanism could not be assembled. Not "needed refinement" — the rack was physically larger than the drawer it bolts into. Every blocker below was confirmed against the shipped geometry before anything was changed.

CheckWasNowWhy it mattered
Rack inside its own drawer154.89 mm³0.00 mm³the flange was bigger than the bin, in both axes

Entry05/ 10
THE GEAR

The pinion was the wrong shape, and a simulation proved it.

Straight-sided teeth are correct for a rack and wrong for a pinion — 0.26 mm of excess material per flank. The pair met with effectively zero clearance and seized at the growth generic PLA actually prints at.

The fix is a true involute flank. The simulation reproduces the old profile's jam, which is the only reason to trust it about the new one.

Old profile, nominal0.047 mmeffectively zero
Old profile, +0.05 mmJAMSinside normal PLA growth
New profile, nominal0.489 mmtrue involute, stub addendum
New profile, +0.20 mm0.089 mmstill turning
Tooth tip0.748 mmprintable at 0.4 mm nozzle

Entry06/ 10
THE TERMINAL

The screen is the product.

PIN-gated access, a live section drawing per bay, a tool register and an append-only event ledger. Every open, close, unlock and rejected PIN is recorded. A wrong PIN returns 403 — denied, logged.

The register says SECURED or ACCESSIBLE. It never says "present", because nothing here senses presence.

firmware/www/index.html · MicroPython on an ESP32-S3
Entry07/ 10
LIMITS

What this does not do.

  • It reaches 23.7 mm of a 51.2 mm bin. A half turn at a 10.0 mm pitch radius is 31.42 mm and there is no more. A larger gear would cantilever the drawer off its own deck.
  • It counts nothing. No sensing of any kind. Neither does the cabinet it is pitched against, but that is an argument, not a feature.
  • Two drawers. This is a demonstrator at 92 × 74 × 66 mm, not a shop-floor unit.
  • Hobby servos. SG90s reach 160–175° of a nominal 180, so the firmware commands 153° and keeps 4.72 mm in hand.
stated because a buyer will find it in ninety seconds

Entry09/ 10
PROVENANCE

The repository is the evidence.

Parametric source, the verification scripts, the audit that returned NO-GO and every commit that answered it. Run the scripts and you will get the numbers on this page, or you will have caught us.

The overhang checker still prints NEEDS FIXING on both case halves. Those are bridges, and they print. It is on the page because softening a script's own verdict is how a document of record stops being one.
